name: a-camcorder-sprinkler-garden
idea: Beat A. A frame grabbed from a late-1990s family camcorder tape: a small back garden in a British terraced street on a hot afternoon, two kids in swimsuits leaping through the arc of a lawn sprinkler, a bike dropped on the grass, a parent's arm half in frame. Medium-wide, handheld, slightly tilted, soft focus with warm washed-out colour, a faint chroma bleed on the reds and the flat brightness of overcast-bright sun. Shot from adult waist height as if Dad is filming. Pure ordinary joy, nothing staged.

name: a-flash-digicam-birthday
idea: Beat A. A snapshot from an early-2000s compact digital camera at a child's birthday party in a cramped living room at night: a gap-toothed kid in a paper crown leaning in to blow out candles while cousins crowd behind cheering. Hard direct on-camera flash blows the faces bright and drops the back of the room into murky orange darkness; punchy over-saturated colour, a little JPEG noise, red-eye on one guest. Close, off-centre framing with a tilted horizon and clutter (balloons, crisps bowls, a patterned carpet). Loud, messy, happy.

name: a-disposable-film-seaside
idea: Beat A. A print from a cheap disposable film camera on a British seaside day out around 1998: a family on a windy shingle beach, a grandad in rolled-up trousers holding a dripping ice-cream cone up like a trophy, kids with buckets, striped windbreaks behind. Wide-ish, slightly overexposed, cool blue-cyan cast in the sky and a warm yellow cast on skin, visible film grain, corners darkened by the plastic lens. Eye-level, slightly crooked, the photographer's thumb almost in the corner. Bright midday.

name: a-glossy-optimism-picnic
idea: Beat A. The shiny optimistic stock-photo look of mid-2000s advertising: an impossibly vivid blue sky with a lens flare, brilliant saturated green grass on a rolling hill, a young family laughing on a picnic blanket, a dog mid-leap, soap bubbles drifting through the frame catching rainbow light. Low angle from the grass looking up, crisp and glossy, everything clean and hopeful, the light high and bright. It should feel like the era's promise that the future would be lovely.

name: a-golden-hour-street-football
idea: Beat A. A grainy low-resolution video still of a summer evening in a cul-de-sac of council houses around 2001: teenagers and little kids playing football with jumpers for goalposts, one mid-celebration with arms out, a neighbour on a doorstep with a mug. Long lens from the end of the street, golden-hour backlight flaring and haloing everyone, long shadows on the tarmac, soft blooming highlights and muddy blacks from a cheap camcorder sensor. Warm amber and dusty pink palette. The feeling of the summer holidays never ending.

name: b-school-photo-backdrop
idea: Beat B. A 2000s school portrait-day photograph: the BadCode figure sits on the photographer's stool in front of the mottled blue studio backdrop, hands folded neatly in its lap, posed exactly like a pupil, looking straight into the lens with polite deadpan stillness. It wears a plain black knitted balaclava with only the eyes visible through the eye holes, black gloves, a neat sensible jumper; no robot parts, no markings on the mask. Soft even studio light from two umbrellas, slightly over-smooth colour of the era's lab printing, head-and-shoulders framing with the face well lit and centred.

name: b-camcorder-party-guest
idea: Beat B. A frame from the same sort of late-90s home video as the family party: a living room full of streamers and a buffet table, guests blurred mid-dance in the background, and in the foreground the BadCode figure in a plain dark knitted balaclava and gloves, holding a paper plate with a single sausage roll, has turned to look directly into the camcorder. Mid shot, handheld sway, the camera's on-board light making a flat bright pool on the figure so the mask and eye holes are clear and evenly lit; warm washed colour, slight interlace softness. Polite, still, completely out of place, and nobody else has noticed.

name: b-flash-digicam-funfair
idea: Beat B. A night snapshot at a travelling funfair around 2003, taken on a compact digital camera with the flash firing: the BadCode figure stands front and centre in a plain knitted balaclava and gloves, holding a big pink candyfloss and a won goldfish in a plastic bag, staring calmly into the lens. Behind it the waltzer and bulb-lit rides smear into blown-out coloured streaks and darkness because the flash only reaches the figure. Close medium shot, slightly low angle, the face area crisp and brightly lit, punchy saturated colour and a touch of noise in the black sky.

name: c-empty-summer-field-dusk
idea: Beat C. An uncluttered calm frame from the end of a long summer day around 2000: an empty playing field at dusk, a single abandoned bike lying in the long grass in the lower third, the sky a soft gradient from peach to pale blue above with lots of open space. Wide, still, eye-level, as if the camcorder was left running after everyone went in for tea; soft focus, gentle warm wash, a faint video grain. Quiet, bittersweet, the last frame of the tape, with the upper half of the picture left clear.
